market_view: VIX is low at 15.6 and fell 15% this week, so this is a calm regime. Oil has slid about 26% in a month, but new headlines report tanker attacks in Hormuz and the US revoking Iran's sanctions waiver. Gold is in a bear market, and chips and pharma sit near their highs.

oil_gas.catalyst: 'Oil prices jump 5% after U.S. revokes Iran oil sanctions waiver following ship attacks' (NBC News) and 'Oil prices jump more than 4% after Trump threatens to bomb Iran and reimpose naval blockade' (CNBC). This is a supply shock with an escalation path (blockade threat). The last close (July 6) does not include it yet.
oil_gas.reasoning: A Hormuz supply shock is a named catalyst. The policy escalation (waiver revoked, blockade threat) could last weeks. The risks are that one-off incidents fade and the jump may already be in the open price. XOM moves only 0.3-0.6x crude, so confidence is modest.

gold_miners.catalyst: none. The '$9 bln tie-up' (Reuters Breakingviews) does not involve NEM, and Morningstar says gold has entered a bear market.
gold_miners.reasoning: Gold is down 21.6% from its high, the dollar is firm and the 10-year yield is near its high. The one-day bounce is not a catalyst, and there is no NEM-specific news.

chips.reasoning: The only NVDA headline is a company blog post. The SOX bounce yesterday is already priced in, and earnings season adds variance without direction.

pharma.reasoning: LLY is near its high, and there are no trial, approval or pricing headlines. The one pharma headline is about an unrelated veterinary device.

copper_uranium.reasoning: FCX has no copper supply or demand catalyst. The small project-stake and uranium-mine opposition headlines do not reach FCX.

would_change_my_mind: A de-escalation headline (waiver restored, talks with Iran) or a quick fade of crude back below 68 would remove the oil catalyst.

handoff.what_changed: The oil slide met a supply shock: headlines report tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, the US revoking Iran's sale authorization, oil up 4-5%, and a Trump threat to bomb Iran or reimpose a blockade. Gold bounced 1% but Morningstar calls it a bear market. The other families are unchanged.

oil_gas.why: The Hormuz supply shock and Iran escalation are a named catalyst at confidence 0.53.

gold_miners.why: Gold is in a bear market with a firm dollar and no NEM catalyst; the $9bn miner tie-up is not NEM.

pharma.why: There is no trial, approval or pricing news for LLY.

copper_uranium.why: There is no copper catalyst for FCX.

open_storylines.name: Hormuz / Iran escalation
open_storylines.note: Tanker attacks, the revoked waiver and the blockade threat. Watch for de-escalation (exit risk for the XOM long) or more supply disruption.

open_storylines.name: Oil price slide
open_storylines.note: WTI was 68.55 at the July 6 close, down 26% in 20 days and back to pre-Iran-war levels as output grows. The shock may reverse it.

open_storylines.name: Gold bear market
open_storylines.note: Gold is down 21.6% from its high with a hawkish Fed under Warsh. Watch for a dovish turn or a safe-haven bid from the Iran escalation.

open_storylines.name: Gold miner M&A
open_storylines.note: A $9bn gold miner tie-up (Reuters Breakingviews). It matters only if NEM becomes involved.

open_storylines.name: Cigar Lake suspension
open_storylines.note: The Orano mill disruption matters for CCJ only if it becomes the leader.

open_storylines.name: Copper to aluminium substitution
open_storylines.note: A slow negative for copper demand.

open_storylines.name: Q2 earnings season
open_storylines.note: Exxon signals a Q2 profit windfall (Reuters). NEM has its Q2 call scheduled. Look for guidance changes.

handoff.next_job: On the next decision day, check the XOM long (10-day horizon from 2026-07-07) against Iran and Hormuz news. Then read the new record for a named catalyst in each family and decide long or flat.
